issue_report: After logging in, my cart shows nothing and I can't add anything to it. Everything works fine if I register fresh, but logging into an existing account breaks the whole site.
expected_behavior: After a successful login the user ID is stored correctly so that cart, checkout, and order operations work without error.
actual_behavior: AuthContext reads data.id from the login response, but the login endpoint returns user_id (not id). user.id is stored as undefined, so every cart API call sends user_id=undefined and fails.
root_cause_description: The login callback reads `data.id` from the API response. The POST /auth/login endpoint returns { user_id, email, message } — there is no `id` field. The correct field is `data.user_id`. As a result, user.id is undefined after login and all downstream API calls that pass user.id as a path or query parameter fail.
reproduction_steps: Register a new account and note it works.
Log out then log in with the same credentials.
Navigate to the Cart page.
Observe the cart fails to load and Add to Cart on any product returns an error.

issue_report: The checkout API returns a higher tax amount than expected when a discount is applied. Tax should be based on the discounted total, not the original price.
expected_behavior: Tax is calculated on the post-discount subtotal: tax = (subtotal - discount_amount) * TAX_RATE.
actual_behavior: Tax is calculated on the pre-discount subtotal: tax = subtotal * TAX_RATE, ignoring the discount when computing tax.
root_cause_description: The line `tax_amount = subtotal * TAX_RATE` uses the original subtotal instead of `post_discount`. The variable `post_discount` is already computed on the line above but is not used for the tax calculation.
reproduction_steps: Create a product priced at $100.
Create a 20% discount.
Add the product to cart and checkout with the discount.
Observe tax_amount is $10.00 (10% of $100) instead of $8.00 (10% of $80).

issue_report: The subtotal in my cart is way too low. I have two items at $49.99 each but it's showing $51.99 instead of $99.98.
expected_behavior: Cart subtotal equals the sum of (product.price * quantity) for each item.
actual_behavior: Cart subtotal uses addition instead of multiplication: (product.price + quantity) per item, producing a drastically incorrect total.
root_cause_description: The reduce callback reads `sum + item.product.price + item.quantity` (addition) instead of `sum + item.product.price * item.quantity` (multiplication). For a $49.99 item with quantity 2, this produces 49.99 + 2 = 51.99 instead of 99.98.
reproduction_steps: Log in and add 2 units of any product to the cart.
Open the Cart page.
Observe the displayed Subtotal is price+qty instead of price*qty.

issue_report: POST /cart/add accepts quantity=0 without returning an error. A cart item with zero quantity should not be allowed.
expected_behavior: Adding to cart with quantity=0 is rejected with HTTP 400.
actual_behavior: quantity=0 passes validation because the check is `quantity < 0` instead of `quantity <= 0`, and a zero-quantity cart item is created.
root_cause_description: The guard `if quantity < 0` should be `if quantity <= 0`. The off-by-one error on the comparison operator allows exactly zero through validation.
reproduction_steps: Create a product with stock > 0.
Call POST /cart/add with quantity=0.
Observe HTTP 201 is returned instead of 400.

issue_report: The website works fine until I click Checkout. The button just spins and nothing happens. I've tried clearing my cart and re-adding items but checkout never completes.
expected_behavior: Clicking Checkout sends POST /checkout/?user_id=X as a query-parameter request and creates an order.
actual_behavior: The frontend sends user_id and discount_id as a JSON request body. The FastAPI endpoint reads them from query parameters only, so it never finds them, returning HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
root_cause_description: checkoutApi.checkout passes `{ body: { user_id, discount_id } }` to the request helper instead of `{ query: { user_id, discount_id } }`. FastAPI declares both parameters as Query params (not body), so the endpoint receives no values and returns 422.
reproduction_steps: Log in, add a product to cart.
Open the Cart page and click Checkout.
Observe the request fails with HTTP 422.

issue_report: The products page isn't showing any of the items I added. I added several products through the API but the list comes back empty.
expected_behavior: GET /products/ returns all products that have available=True (products with stock > 0).
actual_behavior: The query filters Product.available == False, returning only unavailable products and hiding all in-stock items.
root_cause_description: The SQLAlchemy filter `Product.available == False` is inverted. It should be `Product.available == True`. The result is that only products explicitly marked unavailable are returned by the listing endpoint.
reproduction_steps: Create a product with stock=5 (available=True).
Call GET /products/.
Observe the product does not appear in the response.

issue_report: The products page loads but never shows any products. The loading spinner disappears and then nothing appears — just an empty page.
expected_behavior: After a successful API response, the Products page renders product cards.
actual_behavior: loadProducts() discards the API response by calling setProducts([]) unconditionally, so the page always renders empty regardless of what the backend returns.
root_cause_description: The line `setProducts(all || [])` was changed to `setProducts([])`. The API response is fetched successfully into the variable `all` but is never used — the state is immediately reset to an empty array.
reproduction_steps: Ensure products exist in the database.
Navigate to the Products page.
Observe the page displays no products despite a successful GET /products/ response.

issue_report: I can add more items to my cart than the product has in stock. The API should reject quantities that exceed available stock.
expected_behavior: add_to_cart rejects a quantity greater than product.stock with HTTP 400.
actual_behavior: The stock-exceed check is absent from add_to_cart, so any quantity passes validation regardless of stock level.
root_cause_description: The stock-overflow guard `if quantity > product.stock: raise HTTPException(400)` was removed from add_to_cart. update_cart_item still has the check, but the initial add does not.
reproduction_steps: Create a product with stock=3.
Call POST /cart/add with quantity=10.
Observe HTTP 201 is returned instead of 400.

issue_report: My orders page keeps crashing. I open it and the whole page goes blank with an error. It worked before but now it's broken.
expected_behavior: The Orders page reads order history from localStorage and renders each order, or shows an empty-state message if there are no orders.
actual_behavior: When localStorage has no stored orders, JSON.parse returns {} (a plain object) instead of []. Calling .map() on an object throws TypeError: orders.map is not a function, crashing the page.
root_cause_description: The localStorage fallback is `'{}'` instead of `'[]'`. JSON.parse('{}') returns a plain object, not an array. When React renders the orders list it calls `orders.map(...)` which throws TypeError because objects do not have a .map method.
reproduction_steps: Clear localStorage or open in a fresh browser session.
Navigate to the Orders page.
Observe the page crashes with a TypeError about .map.

issue_report: The checkout endpoint returns 400 when the cart has items but succeeds silently when the cart is empty. The empty-cart guard appears to be backwards.
expected_behavior: Checkout raises HTTP 400 when the cart is empty; it proceeds normally when items are present.
actual_behavior: The guard `if items:` raises 400 on a non-empty cart and allows an empty cart through.
root_cause_description: The empty-cart check reads `if items:` (truthy when items exist) and raises 400. It should be `if not items:`. The inversion means every valid checkout attempt is rejected.
reproduction_steps: Add a product to a user's cart.
Call POST /checkout/?user_id=N.
Observe HTTP 400 is returned even though the cart has items.

issue_report: When I click on Cart in the navigation I see my order history instead of my cart. And when I click Orders I get the cart page. The two pages are completely swapped.
expected_behavior: Navigating to /cart renders the Cart page; navigating to /orders renders the Orders page.
actual_behavior: /cart renders the Orders component; /orders renders the Cart component. The routes are assigned to the wrong components.
root_cause_description: The two Route elements have their element props swapped: `<Route path="/cart" element={<Orders />} />` and `<Route path="/orders" element={<Cart />} />`. The correct assignment is Cart for /cart and Orders for /orders.
reproduction_steps: Open the ShopBug frontend.
Click the Cart link in the navigation bar.
Observe that the Orders page is displayed instead of the Cart page.

issue_report: Checkout crashes with a server error. Sometimes it seems to work but the order never shows my actual items.
expected_behavior: checkout_service fetches cart items for the specific user and builds an order from those items.
actual_behavior: cart_service.get_cart_items is called without user_id, causing a TypeError. Even if handled, the call would fetch items across all users rather than for the specific user.
root_cause_description: checkout calls `cart_service.get_cart_items(db)` without passing `user_id`. The function signature is `get_cart_items(db, user_id)` — user_id is required. This raises TypeError at runtime and prevents checkout from working.
reproduction_steps: Add items to a user's cart.
Call POST /checkout/?user_id=N.
Observe HTTP 500 with a TypeError about missing positional argument.

issue_report: Adding a product to my cart doesn't work. I click Add to Cart and it says Added to cart! but when I open my cart it's empty. Sometimes I get a product not found error.
expected_behavior: Clicking Add to Cart calls cartApi.add(user.id, product.id, 1) creating a cart item for the current user and the selected product.
actual_behavior: The arguments are swapped: cartApi.add(product.id, user.id, 1). The cart item is created with user_id=product.id and product_id=user.id — associating it with the wrong user and wrong product.
root_cause_description: cartApi.add signature is add(userId, productId, quantity). The call passes product.id as the first argument and user.id as the second, reversing the intent. The resulting cart item belongs to a phantom user (the product's numeric ID) not the authenticated user.
reproduction_steps: Log in and navigate to the Products page.
Click Add to Cart on any product.
Navigate to Cart — observe the cart is empty for your user.
Check the database — the cart item has user_id=product.id.

issue_report: The discount cap doesn't behave correctly. In some cases the discount amount returned is higher than the cap, in others a discount that should be below the cap gets capped anyway.
expected_behavior: The computed discount amount (subtotal * percent / 100) is compared against max_discount_amount. If raw > cap, return cap; otherwise return raw.
actual_behavior: The code compares subtotal against max_discount_amount. When subtotal > cap, it returns cap even if the computed discount is below cap; when subtotal <= cap, the cap is never applied.
root_cause_description: The cap check `if discount.max_discount_amount is not None and subtotal > discount.max_discount_amount` compares the subtotal (order total) against the cap instead of the computed percentage `raw`. This means for subtotal=30, percent=50%, cap=20: raw=15, but since 30>20 the function returns 20 (incorrect — raw is below cap).
reproduction_steps: Create a discount with 50% and max_discount_amount=20.
Call calculate_discount_amount with subtotal=30.
Observe return is 20 instead of 15 (50% of 30).

issue_report: I applied a discount code to my cart but the discount isn't reflected in my order. The total at checkout is the same as if I hadn't applied any discount.
expected_behavior: When a discount is applied and the user clicks Checkout, the discount ID is sent to the backend so the order total reflects the discount.
actual_behavior: The discountId ternary is inverted: when a discount is applied it sends null to the backend (no discount); when no discount is applied it sends a discount ID (unexpected discount).
root_cause_description: The ternary `appliedDiscount ? null : KNOWN_DISCOUNTS.find(...)?.id` has its branches reversed. When appliedDiscount is truthy (a discount was applied), null is returned, dropping the discount from the checkout call. The correct form is `appliedDiscount ? KNOWN_DISCOUNTS.find(...)?.id : null`.
reproduction_steps: Add items to cart and enter discount code SAVE10.
Click Checkout.
Observe the order total does not include the discount — the API receives discount_id=null.

issue_report: POST /auth/register allows two accounts to be created with the same email address. The second registration should return HTTP 400.
expected_behavior: Attempting to register with an email that already exists returns HTTP 400 with a clear error message.
actual_behavior: register_user queries for an existing user but never raises an exception when one is found. The duplicate insert proceeds, either creating a second user or triggering a database integrity error.
root_cause_description: The function fetches `existing = db.query(User).filter(...)` but does not check `if existing: raise HTTPException(400)`. The duplicate-email guard is queried but the result is silently ignored.
reproduction_steps: Call POST /auth/register with email=test@test.com.
Call POST /auth/register again with the same email.
Observe HTTP 201 or 500 instead of HTTP 400.

issue_report: Something is wrong with the cart totals on checkout. The amount charged doesn't make sense — it's much lower than what the products cost.
expected_behavior: get_cart_subtotal returns sum(item.product.price * item.quantity) for all cart items.
actual_behavior: get_cart_subtotal uses item.product.stock instead of item.product.price, computing stock_count*quantity instead of price*quantity.
root_cause_description: The sum expression `item.product.stock * item.quantity` uses the stock count (an integer representing inventory) as if it were the price. For a $100 product with stock=5 and quantity=2, this returns 5*2=10 instead of 100*2=200.
reproduction_steps: Create a product with price=100.00, stock=5.
Add 2 units to cart.
Retrieve the subtotal — observe 10 instead of 200.

issue_report: Sometimes items disappear from other users' carts on their own. One user reported their cart was cleared even though they hadn't removed anything.
expected_behavior: remove_from_cart deletes only the cart item belonging to the specified user_id and product_id combination.
actual_behavior: The query filters only by product_id, ignoring user_id. The first matching cart item for that product across any user is deleted, which may belong to a different user.
root_cause_description: The filter `CartItem.product_id == product_id` is missing `CartItem.user_id == user_id`. When two users have the same product in their carts, removing it for one user may accidentally remove the other user's item instead.
reproduction_steps: Add product P to both user A's and user B's carts.
Call DELETE /cart/remove/{P}?user_id={B_id}.
Retrieve user A's cart — observe the item is gone from user A's cart.

issue_report: I can't log in even though I'm using the correct password. I registered successfully but every login attempt fails with an authentication error.
expected_behavior: login_user raises HTTP 401 only when the password does NOT match the stored hash.
actual_behavior: The verification condition is inverted: HTTP 401 is raised when the password DOES match, and login succeeds when it does NOT match.
root_cause_description: The condition `if pwd_context.verify(password, user.hashed_password):` raises 401 when verification succeeds (correct password). The negation `if not pwd_context.verify(...)` is required. Combined with B020 (plaintext storage), bcrypt.verify always fails on plaintext hashes, meaning all logins raise 500.
reproduction_steps: Register with password 'correctpass'.
Attempt login with 'wrongpass' — observe it would succeed (if hashing worked).
Attempt login with 'correctpass' — observe HTTP 401.

issue_report: I just registered an account and immediately tried to log in with the same password but it said my credentials were incorrect.
expected_behavior: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt on registration so that pwd_context.verify() succeeds on login with the same password.
actual_behavior: The password is stored as plaintext (hashed = password). bcrypt.verify(plaintext, plaintext) fails because plaintext is not a valid bcrypt hash format.
root_cause_description: register_user assigns `hashed = password` instead of `hashed = pwd_context.hash(password)`. The CryptContext is imported but never used for hashing. The plaintext is stored as hashed_password, so subsequent bcrypt verification always fails.
reproduction_steps: Register a user with any password.
Query the database — observe hashed_password equals the raw password string.
Attempt login with the same password — observe failure due to invalid hash.
